title: The Current of Mount Kessler
premise: Paloma Dunmore, estranged from their archaeologist father and drowning in debt, is given a hand-drawn map by a dying prospector in exchange for a promise: deliver it to the source of the Kessler River before monsoon season seals the high country. The map points to a pre-colonial city buried above the flood line — a discovery that would redeem Paloma's name and settle every debt at once. But the river's source lies inside a reserve closed after a disaster the government buried, and Paloma's father is already on the mountain, hunting the same city with money Paloma's creditors provided. Racing the rising water, betrayal, and their own failing memory of why they left home, Paloma reaches the source, chooses truth over treasure, and ends the story upstream of everything: forgiven, broke, and finally belonging to no one's ambition but their own.
about_author: Dominic Dunmore is a former river guide who spent six seasons running freight through monsoon country before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people who trade comfort for altitude.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. In a rain-soaked port town, Paloma pawns their father's compass to cover a debt payment, then buys it back an hour later out of spite. Establishes the crushing arithmetic of survival and the ache of estrangement. Emotional beat: stubborn pride masking shame.

chapters.title: A Trade at Dusk
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A prospector named Ede Voss collapses at Paloma's campsite, gut-shot and dying. He trades a greasecloth map of the Kessler headwaters for one promise: carry it upstream before the monsoon. He dies at dawn holding Paloma's hand. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What the Map Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Studying the map over cheap coffee, Paloma realizes the source lies inside the Kessler Reserve, closed since the landslide that killed eleven people years ago. The first creditor's enforcer, Brannic, finds them and offers to bankroll the trip — for everything Paloma finds. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma enters the gorge alone, following the river's cold roar. Flashbacks braid in memories of childhood digs with their father, showing where the love soured. First signs someone else is ahead on the trail. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by loneliness.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Toll
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. At a rope crossing, Paloma meets Sefa, a reserve ranger who was a child survivor of the landslide. She lets Paloma pass but takes half their food as toll, warning that the mountain keeps what it takes. Emotional beat: wary kinship between two people shaped by loss.

chapters.title: Footprints Not Their Own
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma discovers a fresh camp — survey stakes bearing their father's university seal. Rage and grief collide; they consider turning back but push on instead. That night they dream of the last fight that ended their family. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Sefa's Story
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa recounts the landslide: her village drowned when a dam failed, and the official report blamed the victims. She believes the old city's terraces were sabotaged by the first survey team — Paloma's father's team. Emotional beat: fury finding a target, and doubt about it.

chapters.title: The Drowned Terraces
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma finds submerged stonework below the waterline — proof the city extends beneath the flood zone, meaning any excavation means dynamiting the valley. They photograph it, hands shaking. Emotional beat: wonder poisoned by implication.

chapters.title: Brannic Arrives
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Brannic and hired diggers reach the reserve with Paloma's father, Aldous, whose funding came through Brannic's creditors. Brannic plans to let Aldous find the site, then take it and bury the blame. Emotional beat: cold calculation dressed as partnership.

chapters.title: Father and Child
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma and Aldous meet face to face on the trail. The confrontation is quiet and devastating: he offers her a place on his expedition as if nothing happened. She refuses, but can't say why she's really here. Emotional beat: love expressed entirely as leverage.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa reads early storm signs and sends evacuation warnings downriver; the government ignores them, unwilling to admit anyone is in the closed reserve. She decides to go up after Paloma herself. Emotional beat: duty against futility.

chapters.title: Stolen Proofs
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Someone raids Paloma's camp overnight — the photographs and the map are gone. Tracks lead toward the upper gorge. Paloma, food short and time shorter, must decide whether to chase or climb. Emotional beat: desperation sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Switchback Climb
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A brutal ascent up wet stone as the river swells below. Paloma nearly dies crossing a washout, saved by improvisation and the compass — now used not as inheritance but instrument. Emotional beat: the body's limits meeting the will's refusal.

chapters.title: What Brannic Keeps
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Brannic has the map copied and burns the original, then reveals to Aldous that his permits are forged and his creditors own him. Aldous, cornered, agrees to falsify the survey. Emotional beat: two men discovering they are each other's hostage.

chapters.title: Reunion at the Falls
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma catches the thief — one of Brannic's diggers — at the falls, and recovers the map but loses the photographs over the edge. Sefa arrives, having climbed after them. Three strangers bind into a fragile alliance. Emotional beat: trust built from shared exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Above the falls, the river emerges from a cavern mouth ringed with intact pre-colonial masonry — the city's heart, dry and untouched, exactly as Voss drew it. Paloma stands in the first chamber as thunder rolls in. Emotional beat: triumph arriving hand in hand with catastrophe.

chapters.title: Guns in the Rain
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The monsoon makes landfall. Brannic's crew storms the site; Aldous tries to claim the discovery while Brannic's men rig charges to divert the river and expose more ruins — which will drown the lower valley again. Emotional beat: greed accelerating past all reason.

chapters.title: The Promise Kept
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma understands at last what Voss wanted: not the city found, but the river left whole. While Sefa cuts the charge lines and Aldous hesitates, Paloma confronts Brannic at the cavern mouth as the water rises around them. Emotional beat: courage as clarity.

chapters.title: The Flood
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The charges fire anyway, partially; the cavern begins to collapse. Paloma saves Aldous from the water at cost of the map and every record of the site's location. Brannic is swept away reaching for a case of artifacts. Emotional beat: sacrifice without sentimentality.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Downriver, Sefa delivers Paloma's testimony and the surviving field notes to the inquiry, reopening the landslide case. Aldous corroborates — his confession the price of being pulled from the water. Emotional beat: justice arriving small and late, but real.

chapters.title: Debts and Ledgers
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. With Brannic gone, the creditors' claim collapses; Paloma walks away owing almost nothing and owning even less. Father and child sit by the river in silence, the first honest silence in years. No reconciliation speech — just the offer of a ride home. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a door left open.

chapters.title: The Current of Mount Kessler
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Months later, Paloma guides small parties through the reopened reserve, telling visitors true stories instead of treasure stories. The compass hangs at their neck, pointing wherever they choose to go. Final image: the river running clear from its hidden source. Emotional beat: belonging found not in a place, but in a purpose.
